summary:
Read/write pointers with a look-back of two: keep value `x` if fewer than two values are kept, or if
`a[write − 2] ≠ x`. Since the list is sorted, `a[write − 2] == x` means the last two kept values are both `x`
already. O(n), in place.

question.md:
In a sorted list, keep each value **at most twice**, preserving order, in place with O(1) extra space.

- **Sorted** input: copies are adjacent.
- **Up to 10⁵ values.**

think.md:
`[1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3]` → `[1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3]`.

When deciding about the next value `x`, look at the kept part. If its last two entries are both `x`, a third
would be too many. Thanks to sorting, checking just the entry **two back** (`a[write − 2]`) is enough: if it
equals `x`, so does everything after it.

approaches.title: Copy at most two per run

idea.md: Find each run of equal values and append `min(2, run length)` copies to a new list.

build: Scan runs with an inner pointer.

lines.text: Find where the run of `values[i]` ends.
Up to two copies, then jump to the next run.

complexity.md: **Time O(n).** **Space O(n)** for the separate output.

walk.title: Walk the runs of equal values and copy at most two of each into a new list.

limits.md: Builds a second list, but the task asks for O(1) extra space. The same decision can be made in place by looking two places back in the kept part.

approaches.title: Write pointer, look back two

idea.md: For each `x`: if `write < 2` or `a[write − 2] != x`, set `a[write] = x` and advance.

build: Keep `x` unless the kept part ends with two `x`s.

lines.text: The kept part grows from the left.
Each value in order (read from the original, so overwrites can't confuse us).
Two back in the kept part: if it's `x`, the kept part already ends with `x, x`.

steps.text: Read 1: fewer than two kept so far, write it at 0.
Read 1: fewer than two kept so far, write it at 1.
Read 1: two already kept, skip it.
Read 2: fewer than two kept so far, write it at 2.
Read 2: fewer than two kept so far, write it at 3.
Read 3: fewer than two kept so far, write it at 4.
Read 3: fewer than two kept so far, write it at 5.
Read 3: two already kept, skip it.
Read 3: two already kept, skip it.

walk.title: Keep a value unless the kept part already ends with two copies of it: compare with the element two places back in the kept part.

takeaways.md:
- **At most k copies:** keep `x` unless `a[write − k] == x`.
- k = 1 is the plain dedup.
- Works because the input is sorted (copies are contiguous).
